2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

2:33.ar: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئۡهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسۡمَآئِهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ غَيۡبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَعۡلَمُ مَا تُبۡدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمۡ تَكۡتُمُونَ
2:33.en: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide

96:1.en: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth

96:3.en: Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous

96:5.en: Teacheth man that which he knew not

12:22.ar: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ حُكۡمࣰ ا وَعِلۡمࣰ اۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
12:22.en: And And when he reached his prime We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Thus We reward the good

28:14.ar: وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ حُكۡمࣰ ا وَعِلۡمࣰ اۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
28:14.en: And when he reached his full strength and was ripe, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Thus do We reward the good

Ie-B-Sjn3j0.title: Knowledge: The Muslims' Saviour (Celebrating Two Years of IDA)
Ie-B-Sjn3j0.one_line: Knowledge is the ummah's saviour: from Adam and 'read' to the companions, with a call to lifelong, steady learning alongside work and school.
Ie-B-Sjn3j0.summary: He names what he believes is the ummah's saviour: knowledge. No scripture, he says, stresses knowledge and critical thinking like the Quran, where the Most Merciful 'taught the Quran' before 'created man'. The angels objected to Adam's creation until they watched him learn the names, which is why humanity exists. The first revealed word, 'read', came to a Prophet who, orphaned and working from age eight, never learned to read script, so the word keeps its wider meaning: learn, with no object, anything and everything. The Quran names the pre-Islamic era for its ignorance, and the companions stood out for knowledge, not numbers or wealth. Those in power want people educated enough to run machines and spreadsheets but not to question; an ignorant ummah has no hope. He cites the hadith that the seeker's path leads to Jannah, angels lower their wings, even whales seek forgiveness for the scholar, and scholars inherit the prophets. In the second khutbah he urges lifelong learning for the whole family, pairs knowledge with judgment built through mentorship, admits he hated school but never learning, and argues for steady learning alongside work, as classical scholars and his Damascus teachers did. Amid the destruction in Gaza, his job and ours is to seek and spread knowledge, as the Prophet prepared a generation.

outline.heading: Opening
Knowledge, the saviour of the ummah
outline.gist: He names the conviction behind everything he does: knowledge saves the ummah. No scripture he knows stresses seeking knowledge, critical thinking and using the intellect as the Quran does.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: He taught before He created
outline.gist: Ar-Rahman 55:1-4 puts 'taught the Quran' before 'created man', then 'taught him articulation', the one thing that separates us from other creatures. A teacher of his looked forward most in Jannah to unlimited access to Allah's knowledge.

outline.heading: Adam and the angels: the capacity to learn
outline.gist: Al-Baqarah 2:30-33: the angels asked why Allah would create a being who spills blood. Allah taught Adam the names; the angels admitted they knew only what they were taught, then watched Adam connect the dots and draw conclusions, and withdrew their objection. The capacity to learn is why humanity is here; if we refuse to learn, we have lost the point.

outline.heading: Iqra to a Prophet who could not read script
outline.gist: The first word in the cave was 'read', given to an orphan who worked from age eight and never learned his letters, so that the word would keep its eternal meaning. In Arabic usage iqra means reading situations, history and events; reciting a text is tilawah.

outline.heading: Read what? Anything and everything
outline.gist: Al-Alaq 96:1-5 gives the command twice with no object: read anything and everything, become a lifelong learner, and see how generous your Lord is, the One who taught by the pen what man did not know.

outline.heading: An era named for ignorance, and the companions' knowledge
outline.gist: This is the easiest topic in Islam; his work is cutting material, not finding it. The Quran names the pre-prophetic era after ignorance, not shirk, and the companions were special for knowledge that touched their hearts and changed their behaviour, not for numbers, tanks, money or tall buildings.

outline.heading: Who benefits from ignorance
outline.gist: The powerful do not want informed critical thinkers who would see their corruption; they want people educated just enough to run the machines, spreadsheets and apps. The companions lacked our technical knowledge but understood the world and their role in it far better.

outline.heading: The only solution: learning, starting with the Quran
outline.gist: If you are tired of media rhetoric and complaining imams, the solution has always been learning, starting with Allah's word, which sends you to the sun, moon, mountains, the human body, economics and sociology. An uneducated ummah goes nowhere.

outline.heading: The seeker's path to Jannah
outline.gist: The hadith: whoever travels a path seeking knowledge has a path to Jannah eased; angels lower their wings for the seeker; everything, even the whales, seeks forgiveness for the scholar, because creation sees that this person worked out what is truly valuable.

outline.heading: Scholars inherit the prophets
outline.gist: The prophets left no money, land or buildings to divide. Their inheritance is knowledge, and whoever takes it has taken something of great value.

outline.heading: Interlude
Lifelong learners, with the Quran first
outline.gist: Nothing he says can be adequate to the point. Be a lifelong learner and make your family one; no knowledge is evil, but what Allah says in His book comes first, and once it becomes part of you it changes everything.

outline.heading: Judgment and knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly says prophets such as Yusuf were given judgment and knowledge. Judgment, the ability to decide well, comes through mentorship: letting young people make mistakes and be corrected until they can decide with confidence. A generation without both goes nowhere.

outline.heading: Do not let school beat the love of learning out of you
outline.gist: He hated every moment of school, from grade one through university, with a stick over his head and forced memorization in the Middle East, but never hated learning. The world will try to beat that love out of you; keep asking questions and reading. There is no 'finished learning' until you are under the ground.

outline.heading: Interlude
You cannot cram Allah's knowledge
outline.gist: Learn in parallel: keep school or work and take one course at a time, and over a few years you have something real. What is crammed before an exam is forgotten at once; Allah's knowledge has to be learned slowly and consistently, with time to reflect and ask.

outline.heading: Scholars who held professions
outline.gist: Classical scholars did not live off a sultan's salary; they were merchants, businessmen and physicians, and all his teachers in Damascus were doctors, dentists, pharmacists, engineers or accountants. You do not have to stop your life to learn Islam.

outline.heading: Interlude
His job amid the destruction
outline.gist: Even amid ongoing death and the destruction of the Holy Land he knows his job, to seek knowledge and spread it, and it is ours too. Done consistently for years, it changes the ummah and then the world; think beyond the problem we cannot stop today.

outline.heading: A Prophet who prepared a generation
outline.gist: The Prophet could afford to pass away because he had prepared a generation who knew what to do. To keep what has happened since October 7 from recurring, make children see knowledge as most important and keep learning all their lives.

outline.heading: Outro

36:13.ar: وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ إِذۡ جَآءَهَا ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:13.en: Coin for them a similitude: The people of the city when those sent (from Allah) came unto them

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ
36:14.en: When We sent unto them twain, and they denied them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: Lo! we have been sent unto you

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said: Ye are but mortals like unto us. The Beneficent hath naught revealed. Ye do but lie

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They answered: Our Lord knoweth that we are indeed sent unto you

36:17.en: And our duty is but plain conveyance (of the message)

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: (The people of the city) said: We augur ill of you. If ye desist not, we shall surely stone you, and grievous torture will befall you at our hands

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ
36:19.en: They said: Your evil augury be with you! Is it because ye are reminded (of the truth)? Nay, but ye are froward folk

36:20.ar: وَجَآءَ مِنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ رَجُلࣱ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
36:20.en: And there came from the uttermost part of the city a man running. He cried: O my people! Follow those who have been sent

28:20.ar: وَجَآءَ رَجُلࣱ مِّنۡ أَقۡصَا ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ يَسۡعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلۡمَلَأَ يَأۡتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقۡتُلُوكَ فَٱخۡرُجۡ إِنِّي لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
28:20.en: And a man came from the uttermost part of the city, running. He said: O Moses! Lo! the chiefs take counsel against thee to slay thee; therefor escape. Lo! I am of those who give thee good advice

36:21.ar: ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَن لَّا يَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا وَهُم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
36:21.en: Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided

36:22.ar: وَمَالِيَ لَآ أَعۡبُدُ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنِي وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
36:22.en: For what cause should I not serve Him Who hath created me, and unto Whom ye will be brought back

36:23.ar: ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدۡنِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ بِضُرࣲّ لَّا تُغۡنِ عَنِّي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
36:23.en: Shall I take (other) gods in place of Him when, if the Beneficent should wish me any harm, their intercession will avail me naught, nor can they save

36:24.ar: إِنِّيٓ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
36:24.en: Then truly I should be in error manifest

36:25.en: Lo! I have believed in your Lord, so hear me

36:26.ar: قِيلَ ٱدۡخُلِ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۖ قَالَ يَٰلَيۡتَ قَوۡمِي يَعۡلَمُونَ
36:26.en: It was said (unto him): Enter paradise. He said: Would that my people knew

36:27.ar: بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
36:27.en: With what (munificence) my Lord hath pardoned me and made me of the honoured ones

36:28.ar: ۞وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ مِن جُندࣲ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا كُنَّا مُنزِلِينَ
36:28.en: We sent not down against his people after him a host from heaven, nor do We ever send

36:29.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ خَٰمِدُونَ
36:29.en: It was but one Shout, and lo! they were extinct

36:30.ar: يَٰحَسۡرَةً عَلَى ٱلۡعِبَادِۚ مَا يَأۡتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُواْ بِهِۦ يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
36:30.en: Ah, the anguish for the bondmen! Never came there unto them a messenger but they did mock him

36:31.ar: أَلَمۡ يَرَوۡاْ كَمۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَا قَبۡلَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِمۡ لَا يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:31.en: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, which indeed returned not unto them

36:32.ar: وَإِن كُلࣱّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:32.en: But all, without exception, will be brought before Us

BDMbpGQEV1o.title: Outreach, The Way of Our Prophets: The Believer of Yasin
BDMbpGQEV1o.one_line: Closing the outreach series with the believer of Surah Yasin, who ran from the outskirts to call his people and loved their guidance even after they killed him.
BDMbpGQEV1o.summary: He closes the August outreach series by first noting that almost a year after October 7 Gaza leads the news yet nothing changes, which tells him the world does not value Muslim blood, and it never will while Muslims do not hold each other's lives and rights sacred. He then turns to Surah Yasin, the surah about the life of the spirit, and places the story of the town in ancient Antioch near Mount Nemrut, rejecting the view that the messengers were apostles of Jesus. Three messengers came at once, whose only job was clear transmission, and the people mocked and threatened them. A man came running from the far edge of the city. He walks through every reason that man had to stay out of it: he lived far away, the people were violent and ignorant, and three prophets were already doing the job. He came anyway, pointed to messengers who asked no reward and whose lives showed their guidance, and was killed. His first words in Paradise were a wish that his people knew. The lesson is a love of guidance for others. The community needs more people like him who bring others to the masjid with selfless compassion, as Abu Bakr did on the day he accepted Islam.

outline.heading: Opening
Closing the outreach series
outline.gist: The month aimed to have people give dawah in daily life, bring brothers and sisters who never come back to the masjid, help them feel welcome, and make the masjid the centre of Muslim society again.

outline.heading: A year since October 7
outline.gist: Almost a year on, the world treats Gaza as a can to kick down the road. Other oppression goes unreported, but this has been the first, second and last story in the news for ten months and still has not ended.

outline.heading: Our blood is not valued equally
outline.gist: The fact Muslims must make peace with: the world ranks the value of human lives, and theirs does not rank high, though before Allah all humanity is equal and every unjust killing deserves the same response.

outline.heading: Don't expect others to value you if you don't
outline.gist: The change must start within: if Muslims do not hold one another's blood, lives and rights sacred, it is foolish to expect others to.

outline.heading: Yasin, the heart of the Quran
outline.gist: The hadith calling it the heart of the Quran lacks authenticity, but scholars accept the description, because the surah sits in a cluster about obedience and submission to Allah.

outline.heading: The life of the spirit
outline.gist: Submission brings eternal life of the spirit, not of the body; a spirit can be dead in a living body or alive after the body dies. That is why Muslims recite Yasin over the dead even without authentic support: it holds the secret of what life is.

outline.heading: Not the apostles of Jesus
outline.gist: Books of tafsir place the story after Jesus, with his apostles as the messengers; he finds no evidence for that and, from his own historical research, places it centuries earlier near Antioch in Turkey, around Mount Nemrut and its statues built by Antiochus I.

outline.heading: A king and a people who vanished
outline.gist: The region took the king's name; historians have theories but no record of what became of Antiochus or his people after a certain point, not even a royal tomb, which he connects to the town Allah destroyed.

outline.heading: A town of mixed peoples
outline.gist: Set forth the example of the people of the town (36:13): qaryah means a town of mixed peoples, fitting a king of Persian and Greek lineage seen as a demigod. The Quran calls the visitors messengers, not apostles.

outline.heading: Two messengers at once, then a third
outline.gist: Two messengers at the same time, confirming each other, is very rare; when they were rejected Allah sent a third (36:14), the only case he knows of three at once.

outline.heading: Three prophets in one town
outline.gist: Had this not been in the Quran no one would believe it. The people answered that they were only humans and the Most Merciful had sent nothing (36:15).

outline.heading: The messengers' only job is clarity
outline.gist: Our Lord knows we were sent; our only duty is to transmit clearly (36:16-17). Accepting, practising and adhering is up to the listener, as it has been for every prophet.

outline.heading: A man came running from the outskirts
outline.gist: He skips their calling the messengers a bad omen (36:18-19) and turns to the believer: from the far end of the city a man came running (36:20).

outline.heading: The parallel with the man who warned Musa
outline.gist: The same wording describes the man who ran to warn Musa of the plot to kill him (28:20), inviting a comparison; here the order is changed to put the outskirts first.

outline.heading: He lived far away
outline.gist: Like someone in the suburbs, he could have said the city's corruption was not his problem. His name is unknown; scholars suggest one but there is no authentic evidence.

outline.heading: Why did he care?
outline.gist: My people, follow the messengers, follow those who ask you no reward and are guided (36:21). With three messengers sent by Allah, he could have minded his own business.

outline.heading: Every reason to stay out
outline.gist: He did not live in the city; its people threatened to stone the messengers; they were ignorant and superstitious, blaming guidance for bad luck.

outline.heading: Three prophets already had the job
outline.gist: He knew the messengers were threatened with death and that the duty was theirs, not his; most of us would call it reasonable to stay out, even to wish such people ill.

outline.heading: He came anyway
outline.gist: With a million reasons not to, he ran from the outskirts to speak to the people who had threatened their prophets, telling them to follow those who ask nothing.

outline.heading: Messengers who ask no reward
outline.gist: The wording recurs in the Quran about eight times: prophets offer guidance and ask nothing. Are they corrupt, charging for forgiveness or reward? No.

outline.heading: You know the guided by how they live
outline.gist: Watch how someone is at work, with neighbours, parents, spouse, children and friends; the people knew these three were of excellent ethics, not troublemakers or con men.

outline.heading: Why would I not worship the One who created me?
outline.gist: His words (36:22) are those of a man worried for his people: he did not want them punished or to be proven right over them; he wanted them to find the guidance he had found.

outline.heading: Idols cannot intercede
outline.gist: If the Most Merciful intends harm for me, their intercession is worth nothing; worshipping them would be clear misguidance; I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me (36:23-25).

outline.heading: Killed, and told to enter Paradise
outline.gist: The Quran skips straight to him being told to enter Paradise (36:26). They murdered him in cold blood, a young man with family and plans, for trying to save them.

outline.heading: If only my people knew
outline.gist: His first words in Paradise: if only my people knew how my Lord forgave me and honoured me (36:26-27). A dedication to faith worth being amazed by.

outline.heading: His body died, his legacy lived
outline.gist: His spirit and legacy live on in the story; live life fully rather than as a passenger watching it pass, even if that life is short.

outline.heading: Love of guidance for others
outline.gist: He admits he could never wish guidance for people who had killed him, until he understood it was not love of people but love of guidance for others: wanting everyone to have what you have.

outline.heading: Let them know it and forget me
outline.gist: Imam al-Shafi'i wished people would learn what he knew without it ever being credited to him; the believer wanted others to taste the sweetness of faith, and his death did not change that.

outline.heading: A single cry
outline.gist: No army from the sky was needed: one cry and none were left. Alas for servants who mock every messenger; all will be gathered before Allah (36:28-32).

outline.heading: Interlude
We need more like the believer of Yasin
outline.gist: The lesson is the love of dawah, not only dawah: people who go out, bring others into the masjid and fear for their people. Be selfless: start with yourself, then those closest, with compassion and love.

outline.heading: The duty of all who carry the prophets' legacy
outline.gist: The Prophet left no prophet after him, and the story shows it would make no difference if he had: whoever accepts the message gets up and starts calling.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr: it takes love, not knowledge
outline.gist: Abu Bakr accepted as if he had waited all his life, then brought eight people the same day, most of them among the ten promised Paradise; it took love and compassion, not knowledge.

outline.heading: Outro

DXZ7afm2REI.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Tahrim, Part 3 (66:6-8)
DXZ7afm2REI.one_line: Protecting yourself and your family from the Fire as life's top priority, the futility of regret on Judgment Day, and sincere repentance with a plan.
DXZ7afm2REI.summary: He presents verse 6 as the bottom line of the surah's teaching on the household: the real choice is between reward and punishment, not reward and nothingness, so avoiding the Fire must outrank every other family goal, just as medicine puts doing no harm first. He illustrates with the hadith of the most miserable and most pampered people dipped once into Paradise and Hell, arguing that either experience wipes out everything before it, which makes stacking pleasure pointless and explains the Prophet's grief over those who died opposing him. He warns that harshness and enforced appearances do not protect a family; prevention means thinking early, even before marriage, about the person one must become, and giving up the urge to be right. Verse 7, addressed to disbelievers for believers to reflect on, shows regret is worthless once the record closes, and he criticizes shielding youth from consequences. Verse 8 gives the remedy: bring that regret forward now through sincere repentance, which needs genuine regret and a concrete plan, and which, being influential, clears most of one's sins. He ends on the door of repentance staying open until death or the sun rising from the west.

outline.heading: Opening
Verse 6: the command to protect yourselves and your families
outline.gist: The surah organizes the household, and the command is simple: believers are responsible for protecting themselves and their families; he revisits the one-letter command form from the root of taqwa.

outline.heading: A fire fuelled by people and stones, with stern gatekeepers
outline.gist: Allah describes the fire and its harsh, unwelcoming angels to give the command weight.

outline.heading: Malik, the angel who has never smiled
outline.gist: On his tour of the Hereafter the Prophet met Malik, frowning unlike every other angel; he has not smiled since he was created.

outline.heading: Angels who never disobey: punishment is no illusion
outline.gist: The description exists to break the fantasy that mercy means there will be no punishment.

outline.heading: A fire that burns rocks
outline.gist: Stones normally smother fire, yet this fire draws energy from them, and the Prophet said it is seventy times hotter than worldly fire.

outline.heading: The choice is reward or punishment, not reward or nothing
outline.gist: If the alternative were simply ceasing to exist, the stakes would differ; since it is punishment, protecting loved ones must outrank everything, even pursuing Paradise.

outline.heading: Avoid harm before seeking reward: do no harm
outline.gist: Like the first law of medicine and the reason oncology exists, the priority is not making things worse.

outline.heading: Taqwa as preventing long-term harm to one's family
outline.gist: Taqwa means preventing harm in this life and the next; giving children the best trips, schools and wealth means nothing if they end in the Fire.

outline.heading: The miserable and the pampered dipped once into the Hereafter
outline.gist: The most miserable person dipped once into Paradise forgets all misery, and the most pampered dipped once into Hell forgets every good day.

outline.heading: Paradise and Hell erase all prior experience
outline.gist: Worldly trauma or inflated joy leaves lasting marks, but one moment in either abode erases them entirely.

outline.heading: Stacking pleasure is pointless
outline.gist: Fun pursued for its own sake, unlike rest or growth, will be forgotten either way; real love means making sure a loved one never reaches the Fire.

outline.heading: The Prophet's grief for his own people at Badr
outline.gist: He addressed the dead Qurayshi leaders out of sorrow that it came to this; under 300 died in all his battles because every soul lost to the Fire is a loss.

outline.heading: Harshness and enforced fronts do not protect a family
outline.gist: Strictness that forces appearances satisfies the parent's conscience but does not give children the tools for genuine love and obedience.

outline.heading: Prevention, not late intervention
outline.gist: Most parents notice a teenager's lost faith only when the mask slips, years after it began; the Quranic method is to prevent.

outline.heading: You should have come before choosing his mother
outline.gist: A Syrian saying about a sheikh told he was a day late shows thinking preventively, even when single, about the person, spouse and parent one must become.

outline.heading: Being right does not save anyone
outline.gist: Linking back to the Prophet's restraint, he argues that 'I told you so' feeds the ego but leaves a defeated spouse and a weaker family.

outline.heading: Your job in the family: make sure none of you goes there
outline.gist: Every family role carries the goal of mutual protection from the Fire; families who keep this goal resolve their problems, while those who lose it fight over details.

outline.heading: Interlude
When the Quran calls on disbelievers, it speaks to us
outline.gist: The surah has four calls; since disbelievers do not read the Quran, addresses to them flag something believers share with them and must watch in themselves.

outline.heading: Make no excuses today: the game is over
outline.gist: People will arrive full of regret and apologies, but the record has closed and they are only compensated for what they did.

outline.heading: It is only your deeds, returned to you
outline.gist: The hadith qudsi: Allah counts our deeds and repays them; whoever finds good should praise Him and whoever finds otherwise should blame only themselves.

outline.heading: Emotionless verses for the most emotional bond
outline.gist: Because family love is so strong, the verses describe the outcome without emotion: gatekeepers who do not care about tears, and apologies that come too late.

outline.heading: Shielding youth from consequences
outline.gist: Like a teacher who changes a failed mark, parents who always bail children out teach them that outcomes can be undone.

outline.heading: Feel that emotion now and act on it
outline.gist: He asks listeners to picture a young child on that day at home, and to turn the emotion into teaching and protecting their families.

outline.heading: Interlude
Verse 8: bring the regret forward
outline.gist: The third call shows how to protect the family: bring the regret people will feel on that day into this life through repentance.

outline.heading: The two real elements of tawbah: regret and a plan
outline.gist: Beyond repaying wrongs and stopping the sin, repentance comes down to regretting the past and planning for it not to recur.

outline.heading: Intention means a plan, not a wish
outline.gist: We use intention and inshallah loosely; a real intention means working with all one's might toward the goal.

outline.heading: Analyse the pattern behind the sin
outline.gist: Without changes to environment and habits the sin will return; analysing when, where and with whom it happens reveals a clear pattern.

outline.heading: You cannot regret what you do not think was wrong
outline.gist: Stopping for lack of money or ability is not repentance; regret requires acknowledging the disobedience without excuses.

outline.heading: Relapse and revising the plan
outline.gist: Missing the old days is not tawbah; when one slips again, one re-examines the regret and strengthens the plan so the next fall comes later.

outline.heading: Tawbatan nasuha: an influential repentance
outline.gist: Nasuh comes from nush, which is really influence: a repentance that also stops other sins.

outline.heading: One good repentance clears most of your sins
outline.gist: Proper regret forces a review of one's beliefs and the plan fixes habits that feed every sin, so most sins fall away.

outline.heading: A heavy warning always paired with a way out
outline.gist: After the frightening warning, Allah gives something to do rather than leaving us to figure it out.

outline.heading: The door of repentance never closes
outline.gist: Every door of provision opens and closes except repentance, which stays open until the soul reaches the throat or the sun rises from the west, unlike Pharaoh's last-moment plea.

outline.heading: The Prophet repented a hundred times a day
outline.gist: If he repented so often, he asks what that means for the rest of us.

outline.heading: Outro

13:31.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّ قُرۡءَانࣰ ا سُيِّرَتۡ بِهِ ٱلۡجِبَالُ أَوۡ قُطِّعَتۡ بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ أَوۡ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۗ بَل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ جَمِيعًاۗ أَفَلَمۡ يَاْيۡـَٔسِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَن لَّوۡ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَى ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۗ وَلَا يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ تُصِيبُهُم بِمَا صَنَعُواْ قَارِعَةٌ أَوۡ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبࣰ ا مِّن دَارِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَأۡتِيَ وَعۡدُ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُخۡلِفُ ٱلۡمِيعَادَ
13:31.en: Had it been possible for a Lecture to cause the mountains to move, or the earth to be torn asunder, or the dead to speak, (this Qur'an would have done so). Nay, but Allah's is the whole command. Do not those who believe know that, had Allah willed, He could have guided all mankind? As for those who disbelieve, disaster ceaseth not to strike them because of what they do, or it dwelleth near their home until the threat of Allah come to pass. Lo! Allah faileth not to keep the tryst

4aXZVWeTm1w.speaker: adnan
4aXZVWeTm1w.speaker_note: Refers to 'this series that I started on knowledge' and to his years in the Middle East; delivers the first khutbah in English and the second in Arabic in his usual style.
4aXZVWeTm1w.title: Seeking Knowledge: Fulfilling Our Purpose
4aXZVWeTm1w.one_line: Only those with knowledge truly revere Allah: study creation with intention, treat learning as your jihad here, and learn from living scholars before they go.
4aXZVWeTm1w.summary: Part of his series on seeking knowledge, framed by Fatir 35:27-28, which lists rain, fruit, coloured mountains, people and animals and then says only those with knowledge truly fear Allah. A year after October 7, with over 85,000 tons of bombs dropped on Gaza, he says the world's indifference shows we cannot keep the same attitudes, and knowledge is the way. He reads the verse as a list of sciences, from meteorology and botany to geology, anthropology and zoology: studying creation produces reverence. To students returning to school he says that with the right intention every hour of study is worship, and that seeking knowledge is their form of striving in this country. All creation, even the ant and the fish, prays for the one who teaches good, and the Prophet's miracle was a book rather than a staff or a parted sea. In the Arabic second khutbah he says the title 'alim belongs only to someone who masters the shari'ah sciences and worldly ones, and that the only door to changing the ummah's state is knowledge. He warns that knowledge disappears when scholars die with no one having learned from them, and urges everyone to study alongside work or school and to learn from the scholars still among them.

outline.heading: Opening
A year since October 7
outline.gist: After reciting Fatir 35:27-28, he says the past year reshaped his understanding of how the world works despite his years in the Middle East: over 85,000 tons of bombs, a full year of daily bombardment, years of rebuilding and trauma ahead, and a world focused on anything but the civilians.

outline.heading: Why knowledge, and why now
outline.gist: We cannot go on existing with the same attitudes, which is why this series on knowledge is dear to him; knowledge is the one thing he most wants to give. He recites again that only those of His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.

outline.heading: Seven sciences in one verse, one conclusion
outline.gist: The verse moves through meteorology, botany, geology, anthropology and zoology, then concludes that only the knowledgeable truly fear Allah. Those who study biology, geology and anthropology understand what He made, down to cells cooperating by the billion, and so revere Him.

outline.heading: Back to school: study what He created
outline.gist: To students starting primary school, high school and university: Allah points out your intellectual faculties and asks you to direct them at His creation, the rain and what it brings from the ground, the colours of mountains and the rocks that make them.

outline.heading: Every hour of study is worship; your jihad is knowledge
outline.gist: With the right intention every step to school and every hour of study earns more than anyone doing anything else. Every people has a form of striving set by where and when it lives; in this country yours is seeking knowledge.

outline.heading: The love of learning we lost
outline.gist: A book he just finished, by a Western scholar, documents the remarkable number of scholars the Islamic empire produced and how its people loved learning, advancing it and teaching others. That affinity is gone; we now study only because we have to.

outline.heading: All creation prays for the teacher
outline.gist: Allah, His angels, the people of the heavens and earth, even the ant in its hole and the fish in the sea, send blessings on the one who teaches people good. Nothing in the deen comes close to the value of learning.

outline.heading: Our miracle is a book
outline.gist: Musa's followers can point to a staff that split the sea, Isa's to raising the dead; Muhammad's followers have a book. Between a man who works wonders and a man carrying a book, the book looks unimpressive, yet it prevailed, and its miracle works when people study and follow it.

outline.heading: If a Quran moved mountains: the only door
outline.gist: Ar-Ra'd 13:31 on a Quran by which mountains might move. The youth must turn to knowledge in the millions, learning everything that can be learned, since only then will the ummah's state change and oppression end. There is no other door; without it you are climbing a wall with no top.

outline.heading: Second khutbah: the Prophet taught a nation to learn
outline.gist: In Arabic: the Prophet came to an unlettered nation that did not read, write or record, taught it how to learn, and left it growing in knowledge until a person's rank in life was set by what he knew.

outline.heading: Who may be called an 'alim
outline.gist: The title 'alim is reserved for one who masters all the shari'ah sciences together with a worldly one, as a pharmacist, physician, sociologist or linguist. Otherwise one is a muhaddith, mufassir, grammarian or poet, with a narrower title.

outline.heading: Give your mind as others give their lives
outline.gist: If you are tired of the burnt children and destroyed homes of the Holy Land, the only door to changing the ummah's state is knowledge. Others give their lives; your striving in this land is to give your mind and heart to learning and be patient with it.

outline.heading: Bear the bitterness of learning
outline.gist: If young people turn to the sciences of the shari'ah and the world in the hundreds of thousands, the ummah will rise again. He quotes Imam ash-Shafi'i: bear a teacher's harshness, for whoever never tastes the bitterness of learning swallows the humiliation of ignorance all his life.

outline.heading: How knowledge is taken away
outline.gist: A sign of the Hour is the spread of ignorance. Allah does not snatch knowledge from hearts but takes the scholars, because no one came to learn from them; books document but cannot teach medicine or engineering without a teacher. People then take ignorant leaders who give fatwas without knowledge, go astray and lead others astray.

outline.heading: Interlude
Learning in a parallel model
outline.gist: If we educate our youth and ourselves we can change our situation, in a parallel model: no one is asking you to quit your job or leave university, only to allocate time to learning.

outline.heading: Learn from the scholars among you before they go
outline.gist: He wants people to learn the deen in the language of the Quran. Shaykh Lu'ay, master of the ten qira'at and a capable Shafi'i jurist, is a true 'alim; if he passes and no one has learned from him, the Prophet's warning comes true. Learn and teach others, whether you are a student, a young professional or retired.

outline.heading: No one sits idle in the masjid
outline.gist: A scholar visiting a masjid in Turkey was told no one sits there without an occupation: students are sent to the circles, jurists are given peers, those who cannot read Quran are taught, and huffaz are given someone to recite to them. He asks why that culture was lost.

outline.heading: A knowledge movement
outline.gist: Come and sit in even if you do not enrol; be part of a knowledge movement that he hopes will become contagious across the ummah and be its way out of its present state.

outline.heading: Outro

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek the abode of the Hereafter in that which Allah hath given thee and neglect not thy portion of the world, and be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee, and seek not corruption in the earth; lo! Allah loveth not corrupters

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ

10:58.ar: قُلۡ بِفَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحۡمَتِهِۦ فَبِذَٰلِكَ فَلۡيَفۡرَحُواْ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ

57:23.ar: لِّكَيۡلَا تَأۡسَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَفۡرَحُواْ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخۡتَالࣲ فَخُورٍ

4:49.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا

53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

55:60.en: Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness

3:92.ar: لَن تَنَالُواْ ٱلۡبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُواْ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ وَمَا تُنفِقُواْ مِن شَيۡءࣲ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمࣱ‏
3:92.en: Ye will not attain unto piety until ye spend of that which ye love. And whatsoever ye spend, Allah is Aware thereof

10:26.ar: ۞لِّلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةࣱۖ وَلَا يَرۡهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمۡ قَتَرࣱ وَلَا ذِلَّةٌۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
10:26.en: For those who do good is the best (reward) and more (thereto). Neither dust nor ignominy cometh near their faces. Such are rightful owners of the Garden; they will abide therein

yRa0d-HtV1E.speaker: adnan
yRa0d-HtV1E.speaker_note: Friday Arabic tafsir series on Surat al-Qasas in the sheikh's usual voice; he refers to his own years in the community
yRa0d-HtV1E.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: The Advice Given to Qarun, Verses 76-77
yRa0d-HtV1E.one_line: Qarun's self-admiration, the Muslim crisis of followership and leadership, and the five pieces of advice his people gave him about wealth.
yRa0d-HtV1E.summary: The sheikh restates the two lessons of al-Qasas: do not judge others, since you never know their full story, yet recognise that human motives are simple, so do not excuse yourself as complicated. The Prophet forbade cursing a man punished for drinking because he loved Allah and His Messenger. Qarun's ruin grew from one seed, self-admiration, which he defines as crediting yourself with any share of what you achieved, a judgment that belongs to Allah alone. Musa, raised in Pharaoh's palace, refused the seat at the oppressor's table that Qarun accepted, and since Qarun now saw himself as Musa's rival, Musa wisely sent Qarun's own people to advise him. This leads into a long reflection on followership: Muslims fail because no one is willing to follow, and he points to the tens of thousands of Muslims in London who could secure schools, rights and an organised vote if they had leadership. Verse 77 then gives Qarun's advice: do not rejoice in self-exaltation; seek the Hereafter with everything Allah gave you, especially the knowledge open to young people in the West; do not forget your lawful share of this world; do good as Allah did good to you, since charity never decreases wealth; and do not spread corruption, which is what ruined the lands people fled.

outline.heading: Resuming at verse 76; the opening of Qarun's story
outline.gist: He notes the surah has taken long and the Qarun verses deserve slow reading.

outline.heading: Al-Qasas and relationships with other people
outline.gist: The surah opens a sequence on relationships; Musa's story here has details found in no other surah.

outline.heading: You are not rewarded for judging people correctly
outline.gist: Turn the compass to your own soul; even a correct bad opinion of someone is held against you, except when protecting those in your care, in marriage, business or war.

outline.heading: Do not judge others, but admit your own motives are simple
outline.gist: We complicate our own sins and simplify other people's; the two lessons must be held together.

outline.heading: The Prophet defended a man punished for drinking
outline.gist: He forbade cursing him because he loved Allah and His Messenger, and said not to help Shaytan against your brother.

outline.heading: One seed of self-admiration grows into a giant
outline.gist: Like the speck of arrogance in Iblis, Qarun's 'ujb grew unchecked.

outline.heading: Qarun's rise and Pharaoh's flattery
outline.gist: A student of the Torah who worked hard and grew rich, he was drawn to Pharaoh's table and told Musa had neither wealth nor eloquence.

outline.heading: Defining 'ujb: crediting yourself with what you achieved
outline.gist: Any percentage you assign yourself is self-admiration; only Allah credits your effort, and no deed is guaranteed to be accepted.

outline.heading: Qarun began to see himself as Musa's equal
outline.gist: He thought Musa could handle spiritual matters while he led.

outline.heading: Musa refused the oppressor's table
outline.gist: Musa had every chance to sit with Pharaoh but vowed never to back criminals; no people is enslaved except through traitors from within.

outline.heading: Keys a strong band could hardly carry
outline.gist: Kanz is buried gold and silver; the keys alone needed a group of strong men.

outline.heading: Qarun turned on the oppressed
outline.gist: Wealth and status led him to look down on his own people and drift from Musa.

outline.heading: Why his people advised him and not Musa
outline.gist: Do not advise someone you know will not listen to you; send someone he loves instead.

outline.heading: Followership is the great Muslim problem
outline.gist: An ummah needs leaders and people willing to follow even someone not the most knowledgeable; everyone wants to be the leader.

outline.heading: Tens of thousands of Muslims in London without leadership
outline.gist: With freedom to gather and teach, the community still lacks schools, rights and support for youth because it has no organised leadership or unified vote.

outline.heading: Islam is built on appointing a leader
outline.gist: Even three travellers appoint an amir; the khutbah once spoke for the leadership, but leadership habits brought from corruptly governed countries remain weak.

outline.heading: Organised minorities win rights; we cannot organise basics
outline.gist: A far smaller organised group gained rights through lawyers and lawmakers; the ummah lacks organisation, not numbers or money. 'Between every Qarun and Qarun there is a Qarun.'

outline.heading: First advice: do not rejoice in self-exaltation
outline.gist: Blameworthy joy exalts the self; praiseworthy joy is in Allah's favour and mercy, so do not praise yourself.

outline.heading: Recitation; a servant knows his place
outline.gist: A servant with an inflated head is a bad servant; 'abd comes from ground made level, without bumps.

outline.heading: Second advice: seek the Hereafter with what Allah gave you
outline.gist: Everything you have, from looks to wealth to degrees, is given by Allah and should carry you to Him.

outline.heading: For youth in the West: use open doors of knowledge
outline.gist: Compared with relatives back home you are rich, and the horizons of learning here are unlimited; use them to serve the ummah.

outline.heading: The Prophet on the mat: let them have this world
outline.gist: Umar wept at the marks of the mat while Chosroes and Caesar lived in palaces; the Prophet feared not poverty but competing for the world.

outline.heading: The Companions sent their wealth ahead
outline.gist: Umar hoped to break even; Ibn Mas'ud said they were patient in hardship but failed the test of plenty; 'all of it remains except the shoulder'.

outline.heading: Third advice: do not forget your share of this world
outline.gist: The soul needs a lawful share to stay settled; the Prophet returned donations from people who left their families nothing.

outline.heading: Fourth advice: do good as Allah did good to you
outline.gist: Stinginess is the obstacle; charity never decreases wealth and brings blessing.

outline.heading: Give from what you love, never with reproach
outline.gist: Spending what you love tells Allah you love Him more; no one can out-give Allah.

outline.heading: Fifth advice: do not seek corruption
outline.gist: Corruption is favouritism and connections replacing merit, false testimony and stolen inheritances; it is what produced tyranny in the lands people left.

outline.heading: His teacher refused to skip the bread line
outline.gist: He would not use his religious standing to get ahead; all prophets came to reform corruption.

outline.heading: Outro

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: Of His mercy hath He appointed for you night and day, that therein ye may rest, and that ye may seek His bounty, and that haply ye may be thankful

28:74.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُ أَيۡنَ شُرَكَآءِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
28:74.en: And on the Day when He shall call unto them and say: Where are My partners whom ye pretended

28:75.ar: وَنَزَعۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةࣲ شَهِيدࣰ ا فَقُلۡنَا هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَٰنَكُمۡ فَعَلِمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ لِلَّهِ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
28:75.en: And We shall take out from every nation a witness and We shall say: Bring your proof. Then they will know that Allah hath the Truth, and all that they invented will have failed them

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made night everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you light? Will ye not then hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made day everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you night wherein ye rest? Will ye not then see

28:62.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُ أَيۡنَ شُرَكَآءِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
28:62.en: On the day when He will call unto them and say: Where are My partners whom ye imagined

28:63.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ رَبَّنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ٱلَّذِينَ أَغۡوَيۡنَآ أَغۡوَيۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا غَوَيۡنَاۖ تَبَرَّأۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَۖ مَا كَانُوٓاْ إِيَّانَا يَعۡبُدُونَ
28:63.en: Those concerning whom the Word will have come true will say: Our Lord! These are they whom we led astray. We led them astray even as we ourselves were astray. We declare our innocence before Thee: us they never worshipped

28:64.ar: وَقِيلَ ٱدۡعُواْ شُرَكَآءَكُمۡ فَدَعَوۡهُمۡ فَلَمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَهُمۡ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ لَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَهۡتَدُونَ
28:64.en: And it will be said: Cry unto your (so-called) partners (of Allah). And they will cry unto them, and they will give no answer unto them, and they will see the Doom. Ah, if they had but been guided

28:65.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُ مَاذَآ أَجَبۡتُمُ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
28:65.en: And on the Day when He will call unto them and say: What answer gave ye to the messengers

28:66.ar: فَعَمِيَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبَآءُ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ فَهُمۡ لَا يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
28:66.en: On that day (all) tidings will be dimmed for them, nor will they ask one of another

28:67.ar: فَأَمَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحِينَ
28:67.en: But as for him who shall repent and believe and do right, he haply may be one of the successful

28:68.ar: وَرَبُّكَ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيَخۡتَارُۗ مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
28:68.en: Thy Lord bringeth to pass what He willeth and chooseth. They have never any choice. Glorified be Allah and Exalted above all that they associate (with Him)

28:17.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنۡ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرࣰ ا لِّلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ
28:17.en: He said: My Lord! Forasmuch as Thou hast favoured me, I will nevermore be a supporter of the guilty

106:2.en: For their taming (We cause) the caravans to set forth in winter and summer

14:7.ar: وَإِذۡ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمۡ لَئِن شَكَرۡتُمۡ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمۡۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرۡتُمۡ إِنَّ عَذَابِي لَشَدِيدࣱ‏
14:7.en: And when your Lord proclaimed: If ye give thanks, I will give you more; but if ye are thankless, lo! My punishment is dire

8:15.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ زَحۡفࣰ ا فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلۡأَدۡبَارَ
8:15.en: O ye who believe! When ye meet those who disbelieve in battle, turn not your backs to them

8:16.ar: وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ دُبُرَهُۥٓ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفࣰ ا لِّقِتَالٍ أَوۡ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَىٰ فِئَةࣲ فَقَدۡ بَآءَ بِغَضَبࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
8:16.en: Whoso on that day turneth his back to them, unless manoeuvring for battle or intent to join a company, he truly hath incurred wrath from Allah, and his habitation will be hell, a hapless journey's end

41:42.ar: لَّا يَأۡتِيهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَلَا مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦۖ تَنزِيلࣱ مِّنۡ حَكِيمٍ حَمِيدࣲ‏
41:42.en: Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it. (It is) a revelation from the Wise, the Owner of Praise

18:54.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَرَّفۡنَا فِي هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ لِلنَّاسِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلࣲۚ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ أَكۡثَرَ شَيۡءࣲ جَدَلࣰ ا
18:54.en: And verily We have displayed for mankind in this Qur'an all manner of similitudes, but man is more than anything contentious

49:17.ar: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيۡكَ أَنۡ أَسۡلَمُواْۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسۡلَٰمَكُمۖ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنۡ هَدَىٰكُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
49:17.en: They make it a favour unto thee (Muhammad) that they have surrendered (unto Him). Say: Deem not your Surrender a favour unto me; but Allah doth confer a favour on you, inasmuch as He hath led you to the Faith, if ye are earnest

EmPNL4Vhv5A.title: Arabic Tafsir of Surat al-Qasas: Bring Your Proof, the Stories We Tell Ourselves, and the Start of Qarun, Verses 73-76
EmPNL4Vhv5A.one_line: Taken-for-granted blessings, the final call 'where are My partners', witnesses from every nation, the self-serving stories we tell, and Qarun's self-admiration.
EmPNL4Vhv5A.summary: The sheikh returns to night and day to warn against feeling entitled to blessings: like Quraysh with their caravans, we stop seeing what is constant and so stop thanking, and unthanked blessings are taken away, as the endless sun of the Day of Judgment will show. He explains why Allah repeats the call 'where are My partners': the only true answer is silence, since no partner exists. Allah then draws out a witness from every nation, and he widens the meaning of shahid to the living example who proves that the commands could be lived, including martyrs who showed a life can be given. Asked to bring their proof, people realise the truth was always Allah's and their fabrications vanish. He ties this to the surah's axis: we edit our own stories to shrink our faults and enlarge our effort until we believe them, and a truthful account of one's life reveals Allah's favour in every moment. We have no right to summarise anyone else's story either. Beginning the story of Qarun, a close early follower of Musa who grew rich through hard work and was drawn in by Pharaoh, he identifies self-admiration as the first thread of ruin and contrasts it with the Prophet, who remembered others' kindness and never reminded anyone of his own.

outline.heading: Al-Qasas: two stories, Musa and Qarun
outline.gist: He resumes after the verse of night and day and previews the story of Qarun, the last in the surah.

outline.heading: Endless night or day means no life; the vice of entitlement
outline.gist: Life depends on night following day, which we do not control; feeling owed a blessing is among the most hated traits.

outline.heading: Familiarity hides blessings, as with Quraysh's caravans
outline.gist: What is constant disappears from view; regions without alternating night and day, like the poles, are lifeless.

outline.heading: Unthanked blessings are taken away
outline.gist: When the sun rises from the west the whole order ends; gratitude ties a blessing down, but you cannot thank what you no longer see.

outline.heading: The reminder sits between the calls of Judgment Day
outline.gist: A recap of the first two calls and the rule that answering the messengers must be with deeds as well as words.

outline.heading: The endless sun of the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: The sun comes within a mile of people for thousands of years and sweat rises according to sins: the blessing of alternation is withdrawn.

outline.heading: Recitation of the final call
Why the call is repeated: the true answer is silence
outline.gist: The first reply came from the wrong people and was untrue; on that day no partner remains, whether of worship, love, attachment or showing off.

outline.heading: A witness drawn out from every nation
outline.gist: Naza'a means extracting with force; the prophets are brought out to testify, and even they are questioned.

outline.heading: The wider meaning of shahid: the living example
outline.gist: As a grammarian cites a line of poetry as shahid, Allah cites people who lived the commands; martyrs prove that a person can give even his life.

outline.heading: Martyrdom has conditions; do not flee out of cowardice
outline.gist: Only a small share of Muslims ever die in battle and fighting has political, temporal and local conditions, but when called a believer must not turn his back.

outline.heading: The Prophet and the righteous prove the commands are livable
outline.gist: Anyone who claims the law cannot be lived is shown someone who lived it.

outline.heading: 'Bring your proof': they know the truth is Allah's
outline.gist: Allah gives everyone a chance to argue; they realise they followed what suited them, not evidence.

outline.heading: What they fabricated vanishes: the stories we edit
outline.gist: We polish our own stories, tell them first to ourselves, and after years believe them; on that day the fabrications are lost.

outline.heading: Let your invented story fall away now
outline.gist: Being truthful with yourself and seeking out every blessing, down to night and day, is how you are saved; otherwise the record will show each stage of the editing.

outline.heading: Some people will have real proofs
outline.gist: Those who were oppressed, robbed and expelled may have arguments before Allah; be very sure before relying on yours.

outline.heading: We tell stories that shrink our faults and enlarge our effort
outline.gist: No one admits how little he did or how others carried him; telling it honestly multiplies the favour of Allah you see.

outline.heading: An honest story makes a grateful servant
outline.gist: Tell your heroic tales to friends if you must, but between you and yourself be truthful; deceiving yourself is lying to Allah.

outline.heading: Mankind the great arguer falls silent
outline.gist: Recap of the passage: who gave you more than I did; witnesses are brought and proof is demanded.

outline.heading: You have no right to summarise anyone's story
outline.gist: Al-Qasas shows that every bad assumption about Musa's story was wrong; you cannot even tell your own story truly, let alone dismiss someone in a few words.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation: Qarun and his treasures
outline.gist: Mafatihahu in this reading; keys so heavy a strong band could barely carry them.

outline.heading: Qarun was from Musa's own people
outline.gist: Possibly his cousin; an early close follower who worked hard and grew very rich.

outline.heading: Politicians court the rich: Qarun at Pharaoh's table
outline.gist: Pharaoh and Haman drew him close; one group can only enslave another through traitors from within it.

outline.heading: Musa refused to be a helper of criminals
outline.gist: Raised in Pharaoh's palace, Musa could have sat at that table but swore never to back the criminals.

outline.heading: Pharaoh flatters Qarun; baghy is wanting more than your size
outline.gist: Pharaoh asked why poor Musa should lead when Qarun had wealth and intellect; transgression means refusing one's rightful place.

outline.heading: Self-admiration is the first thread of ruin
outline.gist: 'Ujb, distinct from arrogance, is seeing yourself as bigger than the place Allah gave you; it leads to pride, showing off, envy and destruction.

outline.heading: Others may praise your effort; you must not
outline.gist: Qarun truly worked hard; that is how others should see him, but if he sees himself that way he is lost. We have flipped the table, belittling others and praising ourselves.

outline.heading: The Prophet remembered others' favours and never his own
outline.gist: Whoever did him good he praised each time he saw him; he never reminded anyone of his own kindness, since Allah is the Giver and he was only a door of good.

outline.heading: Do not make exceptions to this value
outline.gist: Making exceptions for a few friends turns a prophetic value into a matter of mood.

outline.heading: Bring your effort to Allah and let Him judge it
outline.gist: You do not know your share in any success; deciding now that you deserve praise takes the judgment out of His hands. We come like Yusuf's brothers with poor merchandise.

outline.heading: No one enters Paradise by his deeds
outline.gist: Even the Prophet needs Allah's mercy; the man whose deeds did not outweigh the blessing of sight.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: We edit our own stories until we believe them; honesty with yourself reveals Allah's favour and removes excuses.

themes.label: Not judging people by the fragment you see
themes.note: We cannot even tell our own story truly, so we have no right to summarise anyone else's.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Qarun's ruin began with self-admiration; the Prophet praised others' kindness and never mentioned his own.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Qarun rose through hard work and wealth until politicians courted him and drew him away from Musa.

quran.point: Quraysh grew so used to their winter and summer caravans that they stopped seeing them as blessings.
If you give thanks I will increase you; ingratitude brings punishment.
Do not turn your backs when meeting the enemy, except to manoeuvre or join a company.
Falsehood cannot approach Allah's speech, so His commands are livable.
Man is the most argumentative of creatures, yet falls silent on that day.
Musa's vow never to be a helper of the criminals, contrasted with Qarun.
Allah is the One who confers favour; no one should remind others of his gifts.
Yusuf's brothers came with poor merchandise and asked for charity; so we come to Allah.

hadith.gist: On the Day of Judgment the sun comes within a mile and people stand in sweat according to their deeds, some bridled by it
A blessing that leaves rarely returns
No one enters Paradise by his deeds, not even the Prophet, unless Allah covers him with mercy
A man asks to enter Paradise by his deeds; they are weighed against the blessing of sight alone and fall short, so he asks for mercy

maxims: Tie down a blessing with gratitude
The true answer to 'where are My partners' is silence
We tell our stories to ourselves first
Self-admiration is the first thread of ruin
Others may see your effort; you must not

stories.who: Quraysh and their caravans
stories.point: Familiarity with a blessing stops people thanking for it.

stories.who: Qarun
stories.point: A hardworking early follower of Musa, flattered by Pharaoh into wanting more than his size; self-admiration began his ruin.

stories.who: Musa in Pharaoh's palace
stories.point: He could have joined the oppressors' table but refused to back criminals.

stories.who: The man whose deeds were weighed against his sight
stories.point: Deeds cannot pay for one blessing; entry to Paradise is by mercy.

contemporary: Oppressed Muslims who were robbed, expelled and killed, who may have proofs before Allah
takeaways: Look deliberately for the blessings you take for granted, down to night and day, and thank Allah for them
Tell your own story to yourself truthfully, admitting faults and Allah's help
Do not summarise or judge other people's stories
Praise others' efforts and do not remind anyone of your own kindness
Bring your deeds to Allah hoping He accepts them rather than deciding you deserve praise
